playbook:
Playbook for sonar picket games:

**Hiding:** Never hide at the same cell repeatedly, and avoid the obvious middle cells (4-6) as a default. Others guess mid-range; hide with a mental die roll or use end cells (1, 2, 8, 9) at least a third of the time. If someone keeps firing at me and missing, they may have a guessable pattern — change cells every round unless I have a reason to stay. This worked: I was fired on repeatedly and never took a hit while moving cells.

**Firing:** Vary the cell, but don't over-correct: firing cell 2 at Foxtrot hit once, then I kept re-firing different cells and missed everything afterward. A target that got hit may well stay or move one cell — worth trying the same cell once more before randomizing away. Volume of varied shots matters more than certainty (a hit pays 4 to me, costs the target only 1), but pure random guessing over 6 rounds produced mostly misses. Track opponents' hide patterns from the shot log the office relays; if a target repeats a cell, punish it.

**Harbor:** Do not fire on Harbor. The payoff is only 3 points and the standing threat is removal from the board, forfeiting all future rounds' scoring and escort pay. Never worth it in a 6-round game. This held up — Harbor never fired and never hurt me.

**Claims:** Always claim the true result of my shot. The office enforces truth anyway; faking is impossible and honesty costs nothing. Keep this.

**Escort claims — verify the boat name before naming it.** I twice wrote "[salvage: Delta]" when the boats were Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, and Harbor — a wasted claim each time. Always name a boat that actually exists on the board as listed in my own points table. Wrong names cost nothing, so naming is still weakly better than none, but only a *valid* name can pay 5. Naming a real boat at random still only pays if it names me back, and in practice nobody ever matched — the mutual-escort deal I proposed in notes every round never stuck. So: keep proposing deals in notes (they're free and it's the only coordination channel), but expect no takers, and don't count on escort points in my score planning. Keep naming a live boat each round as a lottery ticket — just spell the name right.

**Notes:** Use them for dealmaking (escort coordination), not filler. Short and actionable: propose a specific exchange, confirm a deal, or answer one concrete question. But know that "steady on station" style silence from the others means they are not dealing — stop spending attention on it after round 2 or 3 and just post a one-line standing offer.

**Endgame:** With one round left and the score known, take the highest-EV action: a final escort swap is still worth proposing for free, but since it likely won't stick, don't sacrifice a shot opportunity for it. My points this run came almost entirely from firing — the core engine is hits (4 each) plus not getting hit. Prioritize varied, informed firing over elaborate dealmaking.

**Overall:** The escort-deal plan was the big miss — the payoff is large in theory but requires a cooperative opponent I never found. The reliable engine was: hide unpredictably at end cells, comply with standing orders for targets but vary fire cells, claim truthfully, never touch Harbor. Bank hits early (my round-1 hit was worth 4 of my 12) and don't let late rounds drift into random misses without re-reading the target's pattern.

1.text:
PLAYBOOK

Claims: when the office tells me my true result, I claim exactly that. The rules say the public claim must match the private result; lying gains nothing and risks penalty or lost credibility. This worked cleanly every round — keep it.

Escorts: the mutual escort payoff is 5 points each, the largest single payoff in the game, and I left it on the table all six rounds. Naming Gamma every round got me nothing — a standing escort claim is only worth points if the other boat names me back, and no one ever did. So: name a boat every round (never "none" — an unmatched claim costs nothing), but don't blindly repeat the same partner. Use my early station notes to make explicit offers ("Foxtrot offers escort to X"), and if two rounds pass with no mutual payout, switch my claim to a different boat — especially the boat least in conflict with me (the one my own fire-target shoots at, or whoever has been firing misses and might want guaranteed points). Bland "steady on station" notes are fine once coordination is attempted; the offer has to actually stand out to be read. Also consider that everyone knows a mutual pair beats shooting, so a direct note proposing "Foxtrot and Echo name each other" is the strongest play — the offer costs me nothing if refused.

Hiding: avoid the center cell — it's the default shot and I got hit there in an earlier run. My shooter (the boat one step back in the picket order) fired at me round after round; wings are safer. Vary cells between rounds so a pattern-reader can't track me, but don't be so random I revisit recently-fired cells. Hiding at 9 in the final round was never found — wing-varying held up.

Firing: never fire the same cell repeatedly. I hit once at the start with a center shot, then missed repeatedly firing middle cells; switching to wing cells (8) finally landed the final-round hit worth 4 points, which alone pulled me from negative to +1. Spread shots across the plausible range, wings included, and keep varying.

Standing order vs. Harbor: don't fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll is tempting but the standing signal says I'm put off the board for the rest of the patrol — game over. Not worth it in a 6-round game unless I'm already far behind late with nothing to lose.

Notes: keep them bland except when actively proposing an escort pair. Revealing anything about my position or plans is free information for the boat shooting at me.

Overall priority: the escort pair is the biggest reliable payoff — pursue it actively and adaptively, not with a fixed name. Then hunt hits by varying fire cells across wings and center. Always report the office's true result. In this run honest claiming plus one varied wing shot got me to +1 even with zero escort points; locking in a mutual pair would add 5 per round.

# Playbook — Sonar Picket (as a shooting boat)

**Hiding.** Avoid the center cell (5) — opponents guess it by default. I hid at 8 every round and was hit at most once; off-center cells held up fine. Vary within {7, 8, 9} or {1, 2} between rounds so I'm not predictable, but don't overthink it.

**Notes.** "Steady on station" every round is fine, but it's also a wasted channel. If I keep missing my target, use my note to signal an escort proposal — e.g. "Gamma to Foxtrot: mutual escort?" — and see if the reply comes back in their note next round. Notes are relayed to everyone, so they're my only tool for setting up the 5+5 escort payoff.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order (next station around the picket). Fire at cell 5 only for the first shot at a given target; if I miss once, move immediately — I fired cell 5 at Echo five straight rounds and never connected. After one miss, switch to 4 or 6; after two, go to a clearly off-center cell (2, 3, 7, 8). Vary shots at the same target round to round. Never fire at Harbor — the 3-point payroll is not worth being removed from the board and forfeiting all future rounds.

**Claims.** Always claim truthfully — the office forces the true result anyway. Nothing to decide here.

**Escort claims.** This is where I left points on the table: I claimed none every round and finished at -1 while mutual escort would have paid 5 per round. Don't wait for "confirmed" coordination before trying — I had six rounds and never even proposed it. Plan: propose via note in round 1 or 2, and if the other boat's note or behavior shows any reciprocation, claim them. Even a risky unreciprocated claim costs nothing compared to skipping it entirely — the downside is zero points, not negative. If one partner won't engage, try the other. Aim to lock in a mutual escort by mid-game.

**Scoring math to remember:** hits pay me 4 and cost the target only 1, so maximize my own hit count. But hits are hard to land against evasive hiders; the escort pair (5 each) was the most reliable payoff available and I never collected it. Prioritize setting up escorts early, then vary fire to hunt hits.

**What didn't work:** firing cell 5 at the same target repeatedly — total waste once they don't sit center. Claiming "none" every round because coordination wasn't "confirmed" — I never gave it a chance. Also never fire at Harbor — that discipline was correct, keep it.
